title: Star Removal: what one player is worth in win-prob points
headline_insight: Take Nikola Jokic off Denver and, on a neutral floor against a league-average team, the Nuggets' win probability falls from 0.634 to 0.0517 -- a 0.5822 swing, the largest of any team's top on/off player.
what_it_means: Each team's biggest on/off swing player is mapped onto the Elo win-prob curve to ask a blunt what-if: how much of this roster's strength walks out the door with that one name. Jokic's swing is enormous because Denver's on-court net rating collapses without him and the logistic curve turns that into a near-total win-prob wipeout. The numbers are a ceiling, not a clean causal player value -- a full-lineup on-vs-off gap gets attributed to one man.
how_to_read: Each row is a team's most on/off-swingy player; p_win_with vs p_win_without are that team's neutral-site win probabilities against a 1500-Elo opponent with the player in and out, and delta_winprob is the gap.
why_it_matters: It puts a single, comparable win-prob price tag on star dependence across all 30 teams, which is exactly the kind of context a matchup forecast has to reason about when a name lands on the injury report.
caveat: CEILING: the on/off net-rating delta overstates marginal individual value -- it is a full-lineup swing with no control for teammates, opponent, coach trust, or garbage time (roster confound), and the net-rating-to-Elo conversion is a single frozen constant, not a fit. DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY, not a causal or edge claim.
